title: Justice Department warns California officials about counting some ballots
summary:
The U.S. Justice Department is warning election officials in California that they could face criminal investigation if they count ballots from people the federal government suspects are not U.S. citizens.

In the United States, only citizens may vote in federal elections. Noncitizen voting in a federal election is a federal crime.

The warning came in a letter on Friday, October 16, from Trent McCotter, the acting deputy attorney general. It was sent to the Los Angeles County Counsel's office and copied to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar Dean Logan. The letter says people who knowingly count ballots from individuals that federal agencies have identified as noncitizens "risk becoming aiders and abettors to a federal crime."

One day earlier, the Trump administration sued California. The lawsuit asks the state not to count mail ballots from about 20,000 people the federal government calls "likely" noncitizens until their immigration status is confirmed. California mails ballots to all registered voters. Weber said the administration has provided no evidence to support its claim about the list. The offices that received the letter did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The Justice Department has charged about 90 people with election misconduct so far this year, including 50 accused of voting as noncitizens. More than 227 million people were registered to vote nationwide in 2024. Earlier this year, the administration said Nevada had 1,500 noncitizen voters, but after checking, the number of registered noncitizens there turned out to be zero.

The midterm election is on November 3. California has more than 23 million registered voters, and several of its close congressional races could help decide which party controls the U.S. House.
why_it_matters: The dispute is about who gets to decide how votes are counted, the federal government or the states, and it could affect close races that help decide control of the U.S. House.

keywords.explanation: A criminal investigation is when officials gather evidence to find out whether someone broke the law.
A noncitizen is a person living in a country who is not a legal citizen of that country.
Aiders and abettors are people who help someone else commit a crime.
A lawsuit is a case brought to a court so a judge can settle a disagreement.
Immigration status describes whether a person is a citizen, a legal resident or something else in a country.
Misconduct means behavior that breaks rules or laws.

background_read: In the United States, only citizens are allowed to vote in federal elections, such as elections for Congress.
States run their own elections, including deciding how ballots are mailed out, checked and counted.
The U.S. Justice Department is the part of the federal government that enforces federal laws and can bring criminal cases.
When the federal government and a state disagree about election rules, the dispute can end up in court, as it has here with a lawsuit against California.
